01
Project

The Vessel

A convenient iced tea vessel designed for the fast-paced and hectic life of food delivery.

02
Context

Designing for a moving workday

Food-delivery workers often have limited time to stop, drink, and rest. The project explores how a familiar iced-tea ritual can become more convenient within that workflow.

03
Ideation

From thumbnails to form

The early exploration focused on cold retention, portability, ease of use, durability, and capacity. Cardboard models were used to rapidly verify proportion and size.

04
Prototyping

Model & mechanical validation

Dimensions, tolerances, printed parts, and mechanical structures were repeatedly tested and refined before the final configuration.

05
Engineering

A system of parts

The final assembly combines a single-wall 316L stainless-steel body with a Tritan lid, silicone sealing and grip components, a tea filter, hinge hardware, and a quick-locking mechanism.

06
Interaction

120° opening angle

The lid is designed to open wide enough for drinking while staying controlled during closing. A push-button mechanism releases the lid, and the threaded body allows quick tightening and loosening.

07
CMF

Material, finish & color

The proposed body uses stainless steel with surface treatment, while the lid and grip introduce contrasting soft and translucent visual elements.

08
Manufacturing

From sheet to finished vessel

The body concept uses cutting, deep drawing, secondary forming, edge trimming, brushing, cleaning, inspection, and assembly. The Tritan lid concept uses drying, injection molding, cooling, ejection, and gate trimming.

09
In context

Built around the delivery workflow

A bicycle placement area keeps the cold drink away from heat from a takeout container. The detachable tea filter and locking mechanism support the intended use sequence.

10
Final

The Vessel

825 ml • 11 in • 360 g empty • 1.2 kg full
